title: Partition Tolerance
description: Understand partition tolerance and how systems detect and recover from network partitions.

data.text: Network partitions occur when communication between nodes is lost. Causes include fiber cuts, misconfigured routers, cloud provider outages, and software bugs in load balancers. Partition tolerance means the system continues operating despite these failures. Detecting a partition is itself hard because a network delay can look identical to a node crash. This ambiguity is at the heart of the FLP impossibility result.

Distributed systems use timeouts and heartbeat messages to suspect failures. If a node does not respond within the timeout, other nodes mark it as unreachable. However, a slow node is indistinguishable from a crashed node until the timeout expires. Tuning timeouts is therefore a trade-off: short timeouts detect failures quickly but cause false positives during transient congestion, while long timeouts reduce false positives but delay recovery.

data.title: Split Brain Risk
data.text: If two halves of a partition each elect a leader, the system can experience split brain: two leaders accepting writes independently. Quorum protocols and fencing tokens are common mitigations.

data.title: Steps for Handling Partitions
items: Detect: monitor heartbeats and connection timeouts across nodes.
Isolate: identify which nodes can still communicate and form a new group.
Elect: use consensus algorithms like Raft or Paxos to elect a leader within the healthy group.
Reconcile: after the partition heals, merge diverged state using anti-entropy, Merkle trees, or version vectors.

rows: Prevents split brain by requiring majority acknowledgment.
Rejects stale leaders using monotonically increasing IDs.
Requires external fencing service or shared storage.
Efficiently detects and repairs divergent state.

terms.definition: A condition where two parts of a partitioned cluster each believe they are the sole leader and accept writes independently.
A majority of nodes that must agree for an operation to succeed, preventing conflicting decisions.
A background process that detects differences between replicas and repairs divergence.

data.title: Design a Partition Detection Scheme
data.description: You are designing a three-region key-value store. Describe how you would detect a partition between Region A and Region B, what timeout you would choose, and how you would prevent split brain during recovery.
steps: Define heartbeat interval and timeout based on RTT between regions.
Explain how Region A and Region B form separate quorums.
Describe how to use fencing tokens or Raft term numbers to reject stale leaders.
Outline an anti-entropy reconciliation process after the partition heals.
data.expectedOutcome: A clear detection, isolation, and reconciliation plan that prevents data corruption.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Partitions are inevitable; partition tolerance is mandatory for distributed systems.
Detection is ambiguous because delays resemble failures.
Quorum protocols and consensus algorithms prevent split brain.
Reconciliation after partition healing is as important as detection.
data.takeaway: Partition tolerance is not just about surviving failure; it is about recovering safely.
